A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Compositional Simulation-Based Inference for Time Series. Their main text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments on synthetic Markovian benchmarks, Lotka–Volterra, SIR and Kolmogorov flow, including additional experiments and calibration results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, proposal-construction experiments, training-budget results and calibration analyses.

M1.justification: The core FNSE/FNLE/FNRE procedures and GAUSS/JAC composition remain unchanged. v2 adds an explicit prior-predictive proposal-construction procedure in Appendix C.1 and sketches conditioning on the time interval to handle missing observations and irregular grids in A.2.5.

E1.justification: The evaluated tasks remain Gaussian and mixture random walks, periodic and linear SDEs, double well, Lotka–Volterra, SIR and Kolmogorov flow. The time-variant random walk is retained under the name time-inhomogeneous random walk. Missing-data handling is discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

E2.justification: Tables 3–4 substantially expand the evaluated comparators beyond v1's global NPE baseline and factorized methods. Additions include NPE' with pooled transition-window embeddings, NPE+/NPE++ and NLE+/NLE++ using the learned-summary approaches of Chen et al. (2021; 2023), and nonfactorized NSE.

E3.justification: Added protocols include an equal-budget NPE control trained on length-50 sequences, budget sweeps extending to one million transitions, proposal comparisons allocating 5k steps to construction and 95k to training, and Lotka–Volterra/SIR calibration using 1000 test simulations. These extend the evaluation design while retaining the original headline settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds cost-controlled proposal-construction studies (Figure 5, Tables 1–2), training-budget sensitivity results (Figure 6), and FNSE-versus-NPE calibration across sequence lengths for Lotka–Volterra and SIR (Figure 7). The earlier partial-factorization, composition-rule, proposal-width and Kolmogorov calibration analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 retains averaging over ten observations and five repetitions with different random seeds. Error-bar reporting and rank-based simulation calibration already appear in v1; extending calibration to additional experiments does not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original result curves are retained, but Tables 1–4 and Figures 5–7 add substantial numerical and qualitative evidence. For example, Table 4 newly compares SIR C2ST of 0.74 for FNSE against 1.00 for NSE at 100k training transitions and T=100. These are expanded comparisons, not demonstrated same-setting performance improvements between versions.

T1.justification: The original score-factorization proof and existing mathematical extensions remain. v2 explicitly adds the proposal-support assumption and supplies correction-integral and denoising-covariance expressions in Appendix B.2. This is a limited mathematical expansion; the new JAC expression also introduces an unexplained m(a).

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contribution: simulation-efficient amortized inference through composition of local transition inference, including score and likelihood-based variants and scalability to Kolmogorov flow. Clearer approximation wording and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations distinguishing sequence-length generalization problems from accumulated local errors, hypothesizes that Lotka–Volterra periodicity helps NPE generalize, and explicitly discusses loss of global amortization with observation-specific proposals. The principal limitations concerning hidden Markov models and Gaussian score-composition approximations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly specifies proposal and initial-state distributions for the retained linear-SDE and double-well experiments. Appendix E.1 documents implementations of added comparators, including NPE' embedding dimensions and summary-learning objectives. The repository access information and existing FNSE training and Kolmogorov architecture details remain.

R1.justification: Section 5.1 substantially broadens positioning beyond composition, data assimilation and filtering. It adds discussion and citations concerning learned and path-signature summaries, structured amortized inference, sequential and cost-aware simulation allocation, and ABC approaches, including Chen, Dyer and Bharti and colleagues.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites substantial introduction and methods passages and reorganizes the exposition. Score-composition material is consolidated in Appendix B, proposal construction gains Section 3.4 and Appendix C, and experimental details and analyses become Appendices D–E. The related-work narrative and back-matter ordering also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds four comparison tables and three multipanel figures covering proposals, training budgets and calibration. Existing figures are largely retained and renumbered, with smaller axis, legend and caption edits. Figure 4's caption changes ten observations to fifty, resolving its disagreement with the already-existing body text.

improvement.justification: v1's comparative evidence depended on one global NPE design and mostly hand-selected proposals. v2 tests alternative embeddings, learned summaries, NSE and longer training sequences, accounts for proposal-construction costs, and adds calibration checks for two central applications. These additions substantially strengthen the credibility and practical support for the simulation-efficiency claim. Inconsistent sequence-length labels in Tables 1–2 and the unexplained m(a) in Appendix B.2 reduce clarity, but do not outweigh these gains.
